rationale: Ground truth has no substantive concerns to recall, so both score fully there. X is thorough (greps, reads) and gives concrete file:line/edit suggestions, but several findings (hardware-table wording, pyproject.toml description, demanding server-log artifacts for an already-tested small bugfix) are marginal nitpicks or process overreach that dilute precision. Y is tighter and better calibrated: its pass/fail scan is accurate, its single comment (sm_110a future-proofing) is genuinely grounded in the PR's own stated rationale and honestly flagged as low-signal, and its APPROVE recommendation matches the actual scope/quality of a clean, well-tested bugfix — though it is less concretely actionable than X's specific line-edit suggestions.
